Submitting iteration 10.

**What changed**
- Decoded the eyebrow elements of the three landing heroes via pixel analysis: `/shows` has a red "GENRES" word, `/games` a red H-word (6–7 letters, not resolvable at 18px — top template scores: HATTERS/HOTELS/HORROR/HUNTERS), `/movies` a 54×47 red rounded badge with a white glyph (a "1"+"0"-like small oval plus strokes; best-guess "4K"-style badge). Confirmed `browse_home.jpg`/`new_and_popular.jpg` heroes have **no** red eyebrow, so only the three landing pages get it.
- Added `eyebrow` / `badge` props to `app/frontend/src/components/HeroBillboard.jsx`: a red letter-spaced uppercase label and a red rounded white-text badge, positioned above the hero title at the reference location (~45vh).
- Wired: `Shows.jsx` → `eyebrow="Genres"`, `Movies.jsx` → `badge="4K"`, `Games.jsx` → `eyebrow="Party Games"` (honest, spec-consistent rail name, since the reference H-word is undecodable). Home/other heroes unchanged (no eyebrow in their references).
- Frontend builds clean; `validate` → **14/14 passed**, 13/15 contract 2xx (same 2 intentional: `POST /api/my-list` 422 on empty body, `DELETE /api/my-list/1` 404), 8/8 business chain, no dead controls.
- Cleaned `node_modules`/`dist` (workspace 49M).

**Still open**
- Exact `/games` eyebrow text (reference H-word) and exact `/movies` badge glyph — I used the closest honest equivalents; a judge may see small text differences there.
- The exact white hero title in `shows_genres_menu.jpg` remains undecoded (≈205px, H-like structure on a dark backdrop); my heroes show real featured titles, which will differ from the reference app's content by design.
